notes: The 'in' of 'instructed in the way' stays inside the participle's unit under rule 106's accusative arm: τὴν ὁδόν is accusative, a case English writes no preposition for, so the preposition is the verb's own government.
ἦν takes 'had been' as the periphrastic auxiliary and κατηχημένος takes 'instructed'; joining the two into one unit remains defensible.
τά → 'the things' heads on 'things' under rule 22, never on the determiner; τῷ before πνεύματι and τοῦ before Ἰησοῦ are unrepresented under rule 23.
